headline: Revenue growth and fading IPO costs narrow losses sharply
summary_short: SailPoint's fiscal Q1 2027 (three months ended April 30, 2026) revenue rose 22% y/y to $280.1 million, and GAAP net loss narrowed to $74.7 million from $187.3 million a year earlier, with the larger prior-year loss driven by one-time IPO-related charges rather than an operating decline.
summary_long: Gross profit rose 42% y/y to $181.1M (65% margin, up from 55%) on subscription growth (+23% to $265.8M, led by 35% SaaS growth) and lower IPO-award equity comp. Opex fell 17% y/y to $260.9M as the prior year carried $160.5M of IPO-award equity comp vs $69.1M now; adjusted operating income rose to $37.8M (14% margin) from $23.6M (10%). Net loss narrowed to $74.7M ($0.13/sh) from $187.3M ($0.42/sh); the prior year also had a $15.3M debt-extinguishment loss and higher Term Loan interest, since repaid in full. Free cash flow was $32.5M vs -$100.7M, prior year hit by $78.5M of IPO cash settlements. Cash $390.8M, no debt, $250M revolver undrawn. ARR $1,162.7M (+25.7% y/y), net retention 113%, RPO $1.8B.

No dividend, buyback, or non-GAAP EPS figure was disclosed in this 10-Q. No forward guidance (revenue, EPS, or otherwise) is given in the filing — 10-Qs typically don't carry it; none captured here.

drivers.explanation: Subscription revenue growth and the fade of one-time IPO-related equity compensation and debt-extinguishment charges from the prior-year quarter drove sharply narrower GAAP losses and higher adjusted operating income.
Subscription revenue grew 23% ($50.5M) on SaaS (+35%) and term-subscription (+10%) growth from new-customer wins and expansion with existing customers.
Margin rose to 65% from 55%, primarily from revenue growth and a decrease in equity-based compensation tied to IPO-award acceleration in the prior-year quarter.
Loss narrowed to $(79.8)M from $(185.0)M mainly because the prior-year quarter carried $160.5M of equity comp from IPO-award acceleration versus $69.1M this quarter.

Narrowed alongside the operating-loss improvement; the prior-year quarter also included a $15.3M debt-extinguishment loss and $22.4M higher interest expense, both eliminated after the Term Loans were repaid in full.
